items.note: 'Udayapur, which was an important centre of the Paramâra government, was in the Bhâillasvâmi-mahâdvâdasâka'; a Candella grant of 1134 was made while residing in Bhâillasvâmi.
Candella Sallaksanavarman fought Naravarman and won a victory; an Ajaigarh inscription says he took away the fortune of the Mâlavas and Cedis.
Reverses show 'the degeneration of its military strength' in the early 12th century; neither Naravarman nor successors restored its glory.
Naravarman was a poet and patron of letters; 'He built many temples, though few remains of them can be traced now', with works at Nagpur and Bhilsa.
Sam 1191 = 1134 A.D. grant of two villages by Yasovarman to a Karnata Brahman on the annual funeral ceremony of Naravarman.
Yasovarman ascended when Malwa's military resources were exhausted by the war with the Caulukyas; 'not a capable military leader'.
The Ingnoda inscription 'clearly shows that the disintegration of the Paramāra kingdom had begun since the latter part of the reign of Naravarman'.

items.note: Yasovarman fell captive to Jayasimha; Surathotsava and Kirtikaumudī say he conquered Dhârâ, 'the city of Naravarman', and caged its lord.
Siddharāja's victory 'was more than a mere military raid'; he incorporated Malwa by 'the complete overthrow of the Paramâra government'.
Yasovarman reportedly escaped Gujarat's prison and ruled as Jayasimha's vassal in Dhārā or elsewhere in Malwa.
Malwa became part of the Gujarat empire between V.S. 1191 and 1193; Jayasimha styled lord of Avanti.
Jayavarman freed his kingdom from subordination but 'the imperial power of the Paramāras had already been shattered'.
Bhopal grant indirectly shows Jayavarman lost his throne; the imperial Paramāra government remained without political power for about a quarter of a century.
Kumārapāla's conquest left the imperial Paramāras 'lost in obscurity'; 'There was no longer a "Udayâditya" in Malwa who could offer a strong resistance'.
Under Kumârapâla's governor Râjyapâla at Udayapur in Bhilsa, in 1163 A.D. Vasantapâla made donations for maintenance of the temple of Udalesvara at Udayapur.
In 1172 A.D. Lûnapasâka granted the village of Umaratha to the god Vaidyanâtha at Udayapur, which the record places in the Bhâillasvâmi-mahâdvâdasâka province (modern Bhilsa).

items.note: Inscriptions of 1184 and 1186 name an Udayāditya in Bhopal; Ganguly finds no such king in the late 12th century and identifies him with Udayavarman, a different ruler.
After the main dynasty's fall, two junior Mahākumāra branches held Nimar, Hoshangabad and Khandesh and were reunited with the main line early in the 13th century.
After about a quarter-century Malwa 'resumed her life and work under the supremacy of the Paramâras'; Vindhyavarman restored peace and order.
